A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GenHancer research work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–G. Relocated and renumbered appendix figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIP and LLaVA evaluations, efficiency measurements and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a brief pretrained-FLUX ablation result in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The two-stage procedure, class-token conditioning, LoRA updates, timestamp sampling and continuous/discrete denoisers remain unchanged. Appendix G's two algorithms are identical; Appendix B adds documentation rather than a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CC3M training and the same vision-centric, multimodal, classification and retrieval evaluations. The added FLUX ablation does not introduce another dataset, task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: original CLIP and DIVA remain in the corresponding benchmark comparisons, and pretrained FLUX remains in Table 7. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a pretrained-FLUX control described as omitting the proposed training and conditioning choices. This extends the reported comparison settings. The other additions document existing Figure 1 and Table 7 settings rather than establish that their protocols changed or experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a brief ablation addressing whether pretrained FLUX also needs the proposed training and conditioning choices. Existing token, training-stage, sampling, denoiser-size, LoRA and mask-ratio analyses remain unchanged, including the renumbered appendix plots.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added result does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and existing plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. Appendix B newly reports an MMVP drop of 32.9 to 22.2 without the proposed design choices. Its backbone and exact settings are unspecified, and 32.9 does not match Table 7's retained pretrained-FLUX values of 32.6 and 37.1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its proof, the mutual-information formulation and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. Appendix C's sampling explanation and equation move with the layout but retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: perfect reconstruction is unnecessary, lightweight two-stage enhancement is effective, and the approach applies to continuous and discrete denoisers.

C2.justification: Appendix B now explicitly interprets the pretrained-FLUX ablation as evidence that the proposed design choices matter even for pretrained denoisers, supporting broader applicability. Existing explanations concerning information leakage, SigLIP and LoRA remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies Figure 1's 100,000/5,000 stage-step defaults, parameter sweeps and n=4 versus n=19 denoiser comparison. It also clarifies that Table 7's pretrained FLUX uses two-stage training and class-token-only conditioning. These are disclosures for existing experiments; general hyperparameters and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds 11 cited works, including Cross-MAE, Toklip and Saco loss, and removes RLEG. Citations expand around existing topics, while the substantive positioning against DIVA and ROSS remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording and typo corrections, such as 'denosier' to 'denoiser', and new explanatory paragraphs with headings in Appendix B. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is reduced in size and appendix displays are rearranged. v2 Figure 9 moves to page 14 as v3 Figure 10; v2 Figure 10 becomes Figure 9 with a shortened caption. Their visual content and the table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix B improves reproducibility by documenting Figure 1's training budgets and comparisons and clarifying Table 7's pretrained-FLUX setup. The core scientific content remains stable, so the gain is limited. The new ablation provides only qualified additional support because its settings are incomplete and its 32.9 starting value is not reconciled with Table 7.
